name: AB de Villiers
title: Mr. 360: The Complete Career of Abraham Benjamin de Villiers
lead: Few cricketers in the history of the sport have reshaped the geometry of batsmanship and captivated global audiences quite like AB de Villiers. Combining classical orthodox purity with revolutionary 360-degree improvisational audacity, he mastered all three formats of international cricket while dismantling bowling attacks across the world.

chapters.title: 1. Early Life & Multi-Sport Prodigy
chapters.content: Abraham Benjamin de Villiers was born on 17 February 1984 in Warmbad (now Bela-Bela), South Africa. Raised in a sports-loving family, de Villiers attended the prestigious Afrikaanse Hoër Seunskool (Affies) in Pretoria—an institution that also nurtured his future South African teammate and lifelong friend Faf du Plessis. A prodigiously talented natural athlete, de Villiers excelled in tennis, rugby, golf, and badminton during his school years before dedicating his full focus to cricket.
chapters.caption: Early formative years at Affies, Pretoria, where de Villiers forged his foundational athletic craft.

chapters.title: 2. Domestic Cricket & South Africa U19
chapters.content: De Villiers represented South Africa Under-19 in 2002–03 before breaking into senior domestic cricket for Northerns and later the Titans. Demonstrating remarkable composure and aggressive stroke play against seasoned fast bowlers in the SuperSport Series, his rapid rise through the domestic ranks caught the eye of national selectors by late 2004.
chapters.caption: Making an impression for the Titans in South African domestic cricket.

chapters.title: 3. International Test Debut & Orthodox Dominance
chapters.content: De Villiers made his Test debut on 16 December 2004 against England at St George's Park, Port Elizabeth, aged just 20. Initially deployed as an opening batter, he later settled into the middle order where he became an indispensable pillar of South Africa's golden era. Over 114 Test matches, de Villiers amassed 8,765 runs at an average of 50.66 with 22 centuries. His monumental unbeaten 278* against Pakistan in Abu Dhabi in 2010 stood as the highest individual score by a South African until Richard Levi and Hashim Amla.
chapters.caption: AB de Villiers during his epic 278* against Pakistan in Abu Dhabi, 2010.

chapters.title: 4. ODI Dominance & The Fastest Century in Cricket History
chapters.content: In One Day Internationals, de Villiers transcended conventional batting. In 228 matches, he scored 9,577 runs at an average of 53.50 and a staggering strike rate of 101.09. On 18 January 2015 at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg, wearing pink, de Villiers produced arguably the most devastating batting exhibition in ODI history: scoring the fastest 50 (16 balls), the fastest 100 (31 balls), and concluding with 149 runs off just 44 balls against the West Indies.
chapters.caption: The record-shattering 31-ball century against the West Indies at the Wanderers, January 2015.

chapters.title: 5. Mr. 360 & The IPL Legacy with RCB
chapters.content: After representing the Delhi Daredevils in the first three IPL editions, de Villiers joined Royal Challengers Bangalore in 2011, beginning an iconic decade-long partnership with Virat Kohli. His unique ability to reverse sweep fast bowlers over third man, sweep yorkers over deep backward square leg, and loft balls out of the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium earned him the moniker 'Mr. 360'. He finished his IPL career with 5,162 runs at an average of 39.70 and strike rate of 151.46, including 3 unforgettable centuries.
chapters.caption: Reigning supreme in Bengaluru: AB de Villiers in his legendary RCB colors.

chapters.title: 6. Acrobatics, Wicketkeeping & Fielding Prowess
chapters.content: Beyond his genius with the bat, de Villiers was a world-class athlete in the field. He performed double duties as a specialist wicketkeeper in 24 Tests and over 50 ODIs, whilst routinely producing gravity-defying boundary saves, direct hits, and leaping catches that earned him 463 dismissals across all professional formats.
chapters.caption: Flying across the outfield: de Villiers was renowned as one of the greatest fielders of the modern era.

chapters.title: 7. Retirement & Eternal Legacy
chapters.content: De Villiers shocked the cricketing world in May 2018 by announcing his retirement from all international cricket, stating he was 'tired' and wished to step away while still performing at his peak. He continued playing franchise cricket until November 2021 when he announced his complete retirement from all forms of the game. Inducted into the ICC Cricket Hall of Fame in 2024, de Villiers is universally celebrated as a revolutionary architect of modern cricket.
chapters.caption: A standing ovation: de Villiers acknowledged by teammates and fans at the conclusion of his storied career.
